description: Which changed-file ownership profile a branch is judged under. `scripts/ci/check-phase-ownership.mjs` defines the profiles; this maps branches onto them, because the profile is a property of the BRANCH and a workflow input cannot be one.
whyThisFileExists: P1-27-DO-003. `validate:phase-ownership` was invoked by no CI job: a grep of `.github/` for `phase-ownership` returned nothing and never had. The gate's own register entry recorded that fact in a PROSE comment — a command documented as unreachable, which is this phase's defect class stated in its own tooling. It found seven API source files riding inside the P1-27 Frontend branch only because somebody ran it by hand.
howItIsUsed: .github/workflows/_reusable-node-quality.yml, task `static-quality`, resolves the head branch against `rules` in order and exports PHASE_OWNERSHIP_PROFILE. The FIRST matching prefix wins, so a longer prefix must be listed before a shorter one.
unmappedPolicy: FAIL. A branch that matches no rule is refused, and the message says to add a rule. The alternative — a permissive default — is how `check-phase-ownership.mjs` came to judge every branch against `p1-26-frontend`, including Backend branches the profile cannot pass. Declaring what a branch is allowed to change is a one-line diff and is the whole point of the gate.

rules.why: the P1-27 Frontend working branches — apps/web, docs, tooling, tests and root config only
the P1-27 Frontend integration branch

the P1-27-INT-025 Backend remediation, split out of the Frontend branch precisely so a Backend gate would see it. Listed BEFORE the general `remediation/p1-27-` rule below, because the first matching prefix wins and this one is longer
P1-27 remediation branches are Frontend unless they declare otherwise above
a P1-27 documentation branch changes docs, which the Frontend profile permits, and must not change API source or the database any more than the phase itself may

the no-fake-data guard belongs to no phase — it runs on every branch in four workflows — so it is declared under `repository-tooling`, which permits the gate, its suite and the phase records its counts appear in, and forbids the product source a gate change must not smuggle. Borrowing a phase profile would have declared nothing
the P1-26 Frontend branch

the P1-OD-025 shared private/versioned evidence remediation is Backend and Database work — API source, the storage adapter, the scanner handoff functions, a migration and the permission seed. It gets its own profile rather than borrowing a phase's, because borrowing declares nothing and no existing profile permits exactly this surface
P1-18 Backend read-surface remediation branches — the P1-28 unblocking reads and close commands

P1-16 Backend read-surface remediation branches — the customer-vehicle read (P1-27-INT-012, the [MISSING R4] dependency of P1-28-FE-008), judged under the same Backend read-surface profile as its P1-18 siblings
the P1-28 Frontend integration branch — the same Frontend surface rules as P1-27: apps/web, docs, tooling, tests and root config only
the P1-28 Frontend working branches, same declaration as the integration branch
the P1-27 closure branch records the Owner acceptance — docs plus the guard files the closure was designed to lift, all inside the Frontend profile, exactly as closure/p1-26- declared for its phase
the P1-26 closure branch carries the same Frontend declaration

the DBCR-P1-28-001 Backend remediation Owner QA forced — the damage-map revision made mandatory in the database instead of trusted from a compliant Frontend, and the read field that lets Reception tell `never published` from `published and retired`. Listed BEFORE the general `remediation/p1-28-` rule below, because the first matching prefix wins and this one is longer. Its own profile rather than `p1-18-read-surface`, which would also have permitted the diff: that profile describes new GET routes and close commands, and this branch publishes no operation, so borrowing it would have declared nothing

P1-28 remediation branches are Frontend unless they declare otherwise above — the same rule `remediation/p1-27-` states for its phase, and the same Frontend surface the P1-28 integration branch owns: apps/web, docs, tooling, tests and root config only

P1-28 seal remediations cut from develop after PR #226 merged. They change the evidence machinery under scripts/ci and tests/ci and the phase records under docs, which is the same surface the P1-28 integration branch owns.

A repository-wide GATE change owned by no phase: the ownership gate learning that a promotion is not a phase change, and the coverage floor learning that a promotion is not an edit. Carries scripts/ci, tests/ci, .github/workflows and the phase records whose counts move with them — and, by that profile, no product source.
A repository-wide CI change owned by no phase: the legacy workflow fetching the phase base branch so the evidence seal keeps the --not <base> term in its successor range.

A repository-wide CI change owned by no phase: the evidence seal reading a develop-to-main promotion as the branch it promotes, rather than declining its merge ref and reporting the protected branch history as this phase unnamed successors.
PRE-P1-29 governance and tooling branches: the ownership profiles themselves, the gates that read them, and the tests that prove those gates can still fail. Owned by no lane of the initiative.

The Backend lane of PRE-P1-29. Listed BEFORE the initiative branch so a lane branch is judged by its lane rather than by the wider integration profile — first match wins, and the narrower rule must be reachable.
The Web lane of PRE-P1-29, for the same reason and in the same order as the Backend lane above.

The PRE-P1-29 initiative integration branch. The FULL branch name and not a shorter prefix, deliberately: a prefix such as feature/pre-p1-29- would also swallow both lane branches above and grant each of them the other half of the product, which is the hole the lanes exist to close.

The Backend prerequisite lane of P1-29 — one branch per BR contract. Listed BEFORE any broader remediation/p1-29- rule that may later be added: first match wins, so a general rule placed above this one would hand a Backend slice whichever profile the general rule names. There is deliberately NO broad remediation/p1-29- rule today, so a branch nobody mapped is refused rather than absorbed.

A missed P1-09 DATABASE seed obligation repaired after the fact (first: the platform diagnostic-type vocabulary, Owner decision of 2026-09-03 closing P1-29 W9-R4). The lane may add ONE declared seed file, its [db.seed] declaration in supabase/config.toml, the classification the seed-state and replay checks need, and the tests and records that prove it. It may not touch application source, web, contracts or migrations: a seed repair that needed code would not be a seed repair. Placed after the P1-29 Backend rule; the prefixes do not overlap, so the order is documentary.

The Frontend lane of P1-29. Distinct from feature/pre-p1-29- above and not a prefix of it in either direction — pre-p1-29 branches diverge at the fourth character — so the initiative lanes and the phase lanes cannot reach one another.

The Backend prerequisite lane of P1-30 — one branch per read seam or contract the A0 preflight proved missing (docs/phase-1/phase-1-30/a0-read-surface-matrix.md). Listed BEFORE the Frontend lane and before any broader remediation/p1-30- rule that may later be added: first match wins. There is deliberately NO broad remediation/p1-30- rule, so a branch nobody mapped is refused rather than absorbed.

The Frontend lane of P1-30 (services, quotations, inventory, billing and payments screens). Not a prefix of feature/p1-29- in either direction, so the two phases cannot reach one another. The A0 preflight itself travels on this lane: it adds these profiles (tooling, tests) and the read-surface matrix (docs), and no screen.

Every planning branch in this repository is documentation-only by construction, so one bare-prefix rule is honest where a rule per phase would be the same declaration copied. It resolves the two live planning branches, which matched NO rule before this and could not have opened a pull request. If a future planning branch ever needs to be judged differently, a longer prefix listed ABOVE this one is the mechanism — never a widening of this profile.
